Wikipedia: “He once trained under Lan Ying”

bio.text: [Chen Hongshou] was altogether a [painter] who stood apart [and] followed ideals quite different from [those] of most of his contemporaries, a great draughtsman and a [highly] imaginative illustrator.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V

bio.text: About 1640 he [went] to Peking, and two years later he enrolled as a student in the Imperial Academy … He returned to his home in 1643 and when Nanking fell to the Manchus (1645) he entered the Buddhist priesthood, fleeing to the mountains in 1646, possibly in consequence of some anti-Manchu activities.

source.author: Fang Chao-ying
source.title: Ch‘ên Hung-shou
source.publisher: in Arthur W. Hummel (ed.), Eminent Chinese of the Ch‘ing Period, vol. I, US Government Printing Office (Internet Archive scan)

bio.text: He painted figures of very imposing appearance, drawing the folds of their costumes … His natural vigour was extraordinary … For three hundred years there [had] been no painter equal [to] him.

source.author: Zhang Geng (Chang Kêng)
source.title: Guochao huazheng lu (Kuo-ch‘ao hua-cheng lu)
source.publisher: translated in Osvald Sirén, Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (Lund Humphries, 1958; Internet Archive scan)
